newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Robust gains in heavyweight industrial stocks, fomented by futures-basket trading, led South African shares up to the close as the market ignored the impact of a nationwide strike by the country's biggest union.
It also managed to shrug off early losses in index-linked stocks Sappi, which dropped in response to poor year results, and SA Breweries -- down as the firm went ex-dividend.

Futures traders said a number of buyers entered the derivatives market following a large options deal. Contract prices were pushed above fair value opening up arbitrage buying opportunities in the spot market.
"Buying was mainly local, but there were also some foreigners around," a trader said.
The industrial index finished up 50.2 points to 8,290.4 as the industrial near-month futures contract held at 7,950/54 from 7,910 in late trade.

Overall turnover was subdued at around 371 million rand's worth as some players hung on the sidelines as members of the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) protested against new employment legislation.
Cosatu said over two million workers reponded to its strike call.
At a press conference, which took place after the close of the stock market, the union threatened another strike unless business responded to labour's demands for new legislation within 14 days.

Key stock movers included electronics firm Usko which traded over five million shares on rumours of a takeover. Dairy group Bonnita was one of the day's worst performers losing 20 percent of its value to 240 cents on a dip in year earnings.

Recently-unbundled and now focused packaging group Malbak and tobacco-to-packaging Remgro both rose on talk that Remgro, up 95 cents to 45.95 rand, may take over Malbak, which gained 26 cents to 680 cents.
Vierfontein was the biggest percentage gainer on Monday, jumping over 41 percent to 85 cents following a cautionary that a new business might be put into it.
Sappi ended off just 25 cents at 40.75 rand, clawing back from a 200 cent fall. SAB was up 50 cents at 126.25 rand.
Dealers said stock gains on Monday were also in response to a hefty slide in industrials on Friday on expectations of a weak Wall Street, which went on to end flat.

But gold shares had another lacklustre day as bullion dipped below $344, pushing the index to yet another fresh four year closing low at 1,166.6 -- a fall of 7.6 points. The near-month gold futures contract was last at 812/25 from 828.
On the day the overall index ended up 39.6 points at 7,061.3 with the all-share June futures contract at 6,360/70 from 6,345.
The market was seen eyeing Wall Street overnight which, although starting higher suddenly went weaker.
